title: U.S. House · Pennsylvania's 16th Congressional District
area: Northwestern Pennsylvania, including Erie, Butler, and Mercer counties.

context.text: Incumbent Republican Mike Kelly and Democrat Justin Wagner each advanced from their May 19, 2026 primaries.

candidates.name: Mike Kelly
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2011); Chair, House Ways and Means Subcommittee on Tax

summary.text: Mike Kelly is the Republican incumbent for Pennsylvania's 16th District. A Butler, Pennsylvania auto dealer who served on the Butler School Board and Butler City Council, he was first elected to Congress in 2010 and sits on the Ways and Means Committee, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Tax. He is seeking re-election in 2026.

background.text: Born in Pittsburgh in 1948 and raised in Butler, Pennsylvania, where, according to his official biography, he has lived for more than 50 years.
Graduated from Butler High School in 1966 and attended the University of Notre Dame on a football and academic scholarship, earning a bachelor's degree in 1970.

Returned to Butler after college to work at Kelly Chevrolet-Cadillac, a dealership his father founded in the early 1950s; he took ownership in the mid-1990s and added Hyundai and Kia franchises, according to his official biography.

Served on the Butler School Board from 1992 to 1995 and on the Butler City Council from 2006 to 2009; he also sat on the boards of local civic bodies including the Housing Authority and Redevelopment Authority of Butler County.

According to his official biography, he decided to run for Congress in 2009 after a General Motors restructuring threatened his dealership's Cadillac franchise; he went to arbitration and won, and ran for Congress the following year.
First elected in 2010 and sworn in on January 5, 2011, initially for Pennsylvania's 3rd District; he has represented the 16th District since January 3, 2019.
Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means and, per his official page, chairs its Subcommittee on Tax; Ballotpedia also lists him on the committee's Health Subcommittee.

His official biography lists him as Republican chair of several caucuses, including the Congressional Korea Caucus, the House Automotive Caucus and the Childhood Cancer Caucus, and as an appointed member of the President's Export Council.

His official biography says he and his wife, Victoria, a former elementary school teacher, have four children and ten grandchildren, and that he founded the Butler Quarterback Club and the Golden Tornado Scholastic Foundation, which provide educational programs in the Butler Area School District.

positions.summary: Voted no on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2021, which sought to require background checks on private firearm transfers.
Voted yes on the Pain-Capable Unborn Child Protection Act, which would restrict abortion later in pregnancy.
Voted no on the American Dream and Promise Act of 2021, which provided a path to permanent residency for certain unauthorized immigrants and TPS/DED holders.

record.text: Chairs the House Ways and Means Committee's Subcommittee on Tax for the 2025–2026 term; also serves on the Health subcommittee. Previously served on Ways and Means' Tax and Oversight subcommittees in prior terms.
Voted no on the Bipartisan Background Checks Act of 2021 (H.R. 8), which passed the House 227–203.
Voted no on passage of the American Dream and Promise Act of 2021 (H.R. 6), which passed the House 228–197 (Roll Call 91).
Voted no on the Inflation Reduction Act of 2022 (H.R. 5376), which passed the House 220–207 and was signed into law.

summary.text: Justin Wagner is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 16th District. According to his campaign website, he is an Army veteran who served in Iraq in 2006 and a senior automation engineer who has worked for NASA, Boeing, Ford and the City of Seattle. He is running on veterans and labor issues, affordability, health care access, and school resources.

background.text: According to his campaign website, he was born and raised in Greenville and Transfer, Pennsylvania, where his family had lived for eight generations, and he began working at age 15.
Graduated from Reynolds High School in 1998, then attended ITT Technical Institute and took additional classes at Youngstown State University, per his campaign website.

Joined the Army after completing his education, trained at Fort Jackson and Fort Rucker, served in South Korea with the 6th Cavalry and stateside with the 4th Infantry Division, and deployed to Iraq in 2006 in support of Operation Iraqi Freedom.
Continued service in the Army Reserves with the 377th Engineer Company in Butler, Pennsylvania.

Has worked as a senior automation engineer for 15 years, beginning with the commissioning of a new steel plant in Youngstown, Ohio, and including work for NASA, Boeing, Ford, and the City of Seattle's water and wastewater treatment system; currently works in the life sciences industry; is a past member of the UAW and IBEW unions.

His campaign website says he and his wife, Amanda, an Army veteran, have been married 21 years and have four daughters who have been home-schooled; he coaches youth hockey and plays in a local band and his church's worship group.
Advanced from the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary to the November general election, according to Ballotpedia.

priorities.text: Says he is running to fight for local veterans and labor, affordability and opportunity for working families, access to healthcare, and school funding.
priorities.quote: I believe Western Pennsylvania deserves real representation-someone who will fight for local veterans and labor, for affordability and opportunity for working families, to ensure all of us have access to healthcare, and ensure every school has the tools they need to prepare the next generation.

priorities.text: Describes himself as pro-union and pro-worker, and says he will take on corporate power and corruption.
priorities.quote: Western Pennsylvania needs a fighter. Not a politician who plays tough on TV — but someone who takes on corporate power and corruption head-on. Veteran. Engineer. Pro-Union. Pro-Worker. Ready to fight for PA-16.
